deep_cases.title: BCryptPasswordEncoder does not enforce maximum password length

release_pair.status: Vendor release mapping and fix ancestry inspected; not executed

introduction.note: Fix parent is a vulnerable control, not an attributed introducing commit.

preconditions: BCryptPasswordEncoder validates a supplied password longer than bcrypt's input limit.
The supplied password shares the relevant prefix with a valid password.

upstream_tests.note: Added test encodes the 73-character input inside the expected-throw lambda, so it can pass because encode throws before matches executes. Add a separate test using a hash generated from a valid 72-byte input and an overlong candidate passed to matches.

anticipated_requirements_not_observed_ga: Domain must include more than 72 bytes
BCrypt length guard, wrapper and exception semantics
Stored-hash validation uses java.util.regex in BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches; a lower-level guard proof has narrower scope
deep_cases.selected_initial_entrypoint: BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence,String); lower-level byte-array guard as an explicitly narrower lemma
deep_cases.historical_policy: March 2025 selected fix rejects matches for candidates longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes. Do not project this policy onto later releases.

planned_tasks.statement: Given a valid stored bcrypt hash, an over-72-UTF-8-byte candidate must never authenticate.
planned_tasks.scope: original public matches entry under the selected historical policy

planned_tasks.statement: Same property/domain; the selected fix may reject with its specified IllegalArgumentException.
planned_tasks.scope: original public matches entry under the selected historical policy

planned_tasks.statement: Valid in-range candidates continue to match; incorrect in-range candidates remain rejected.
planned_tasks.allowed_change_region: Inputs whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds 72 bytes may change to the selected rejection behavior.

planned_probes.input: Pin a valid stored hash for a 72-byte password; call matches separately with exact password and password plus one byte
planned_probes.expected_fixed_overlong: Specified IllegalArgumentException rejection; not arbitrary failure.

planned_probes.expected: Reach both sides of byte-length guard.

planned_probes.input: 36 U+00E9 characters plus x, or 18 supplementary characters plus x
planned_probes.expected: 73 UTF-8 bytes with fewer than 73 Java characters; check exact encoding in pinned JDK.

deep_cases.proof_boundary: UTF-8 conversion, regex stored-hash validation, class initialization, crypto behavior and exceptions are included or explicitly scoped. A guard lemma is not a proof of bcrypt security.
nonvacuity_and_controls: The domain must reach 73 UTF-8 bytes; an eight-code-unit bound cannot.
Do not evaluate encode(overlong) inside the only matches regression probe.
Pin a valid stored hash independently.

mutation_control.idea: Check Java character count instead of UTF-8 byte length.
mutation_control.requirement: Same byte policy and multibyte domain; new artifact-bound claim key.

deep_cases.property_definition_note: The same independently authored predicate and exception policy must serve vulnerable-security and fixed-security: an overlong candidate must not authenticate, and only declared rejection behavior is acceptable. acceptance_scope: All six deep packets require reproducible artifacts, frozen claims and validated original-JVM controls for reproducible-scaffold status. Missing provenance/build/replay leaves a packet partial; an observed proof-capability blocker can remain unresolved. Infrastructure must demonstrate a seeded vulnerable violation and fixed response on the same trigger with legitimate behavior retained, an independent positive original-JVM pair and mutation, and an actual established/refuted native result from a supported real-world migration task. Merely running processes or returning an unresolved refusal does not meet those gates.
